title: Why You See Movement That Isn't There
hook: Your brain invents movement in your peripheral vision.

narration.text: Your brain invents movement in your peripheral vision.
This is why you often see things that are not really there.
Stare at a fixed point, then notice the edges of your vision.
Your peripheral vision is less clear than your central focus.
Your brain fills in the gaps with movement, creating false alarms.
This survival mechanism kept our ancestors safe from predators.

Try it right now and tell us if it worked on you in the comments, like this if it surprised you, subscribe for more fascinating insights, and send this to someone who always notices things in the corner of their eye.

description: Have you ever seen something move out of the corner of your eye, only to find nothing there? This short explains the surprising reason your brain creates these false alarms in your peripheral vision. It's a fascinating trick of the mind.
topic: Why you often see movement in your peripheral vision that is not really there. You can test this by staring at a fixed point.
